name: CRS-29 Resupply Mission
description: SpaceX's 29th resupply mission to the International Space Station, delivering cargo and experiments to support the crew aboard the ISS.

name: Starlink Group 6-1
description: Launch of the sixth group of Starlink satellites to expand global internet coverage. Falcon 9 deployed 60 Starlink satellites into low Earth orbit.

name: Axiom Space Mission 3
description: Third crewed commercial space station mission with Axiom Space. Four private astronauts traveled to the ISS for research and maintenance operations.

name: GPS III Space Vehicle 06
description: Launch of the sixth next-generation GPS satellite for the U.S. Space Force. These satellites provide enhanced military and civilian navigation services.

name: WorldView Legion Mission
description: Launch of high-resolution Earth imaging satellites for Maxar Technologies. These satellites provide detailed satellite imagery for commercial and government applications.

name: Transporter-7 Rideshare
description: The seventh dedicated rideshare mission deploying 115+ small satellites and payloads. This cost-effective launch enables startups to reach orbit.

name: USSF-67 National Security Mission
description: Launch of classified U.S. Space Force payload using Falcon Heavy. The triple-core rocket delivered a national security satellite to geosynchronous orbit.

name: Viasat-3 Americas
description: Launch of the advanced Viasat-3 broadband satellite. Falcon Heavy delivered the massive telecommunications satellite to geosynchronous orbit for global internet coverage.

name: USSF-44 Space Force Mission
description: U.S. Space Force national security space launch utilizing Falcon Heavy's heavy-lift capability. Payload deployed to high-energy transfer orbit.

name: Starship Integrated Flight Test 1
description: First integrated flight test of the fully stacked Starship vehicle. Despite RUD (rapid unscheduled disassembly), the test achieved valuable data for vehicle development.

name: Starship Integrated Flight Test 2
description: Second integrated flight test with improved Booster and Ship. The vehicle reached space and completed a controlled reentry and ocean splashdown.

name: Starship Integrated Flight Test 3
description: Third integrated flight test demonstrating continuous improvements. Ship hot staging was achieved, advancing toward engine separation in space.

name: Starship Integrated Flight Test 4
description: Fourth test flight achieving booster catch attempt and advanced Ship testing. Represented significant progress toward orbital refueling capability.

name: Crew-7 Dragon Crewed Mission
description: Launch of four astronauts on Crew Dragon for a six-month expedition to the International Space Station. Falcon 9 delivered the capsule to orbit.

name: Palantir StarShield-5
description: Launch of synthetic aperture radar imaging satellite for national security. Falcon 9 delivered the advanced reconnaissance spacecraft to polar orbit.

name: Intelsat 901 Relocation
description: Launch of Intelsat 901 telecommunications satellite. The mission involved relocating the satellite to a new orbital slot for improved service coverage.

name: Falcon Heavy Demo Flight
description: The maiden flight of Falcon Heavy, then the world's most powerful operational rocket. The demo flight famously carried Elon Musk's Tesla Roadster as a test payload and closed with the simultaneous landing of both side boosters back at Cape Canaveral.

name: Crew Dragon Demo-1
description: The first uncrewed test flight of the Crew Dragon spacecraft, which autonomously docked with the International Space Station and returned safely to Earth, clearing the way for astronauts to fly on the vehicle.

name: Crew Dragon Demo-2
description: The first crewed launch of Crew Dragon, carrying NASA astronauts Bob Behnken and Doug Hurley to the ISS. It marked the return of human spaceflight launches from American soil after nearly a decade.

name: Inspiration4
description: The first orbital spaceflight crewed entirely by private citizens. A four-person crew spent three days circling the Earth aboard Crew Dragon while raising money for St. Jude Children's Research Hospital.

name: DART (Double Asteroid Redirection Test)
description: A NASA planetary defense mission that intentionally crashed a spacecraft into the asteroid moonlet Dimorphos, successfully demonstrating that a kinetic impactor can alter an asteroid's orbit.

name: IXPE (Imaging X-ray Polarimetry Explorer)
description: Launch of a NASA space telescope designed to study X-rays from some of the most extreme objects in the universe, including black holes, neutron stars, and supernova remnants.

name: Axiom Mission 1
description: The first fully private crewed mission to the International Space Station, carrying a commander and three paying crew members for roughly ten days of research and commercial activities in orbit.

name: EchoStar 24 (Jupiter 3)
description: Falcon Heavy delivered one of the largest commercial communications satellites ever built to geostationary orbit, boosting broadband capacity for EchoStar's Jupiter satellite fleet.

name: Euclid Space Telescope
description: Launch of the European Space Agency's Euclid observatory, tasked with mapping billions of galaxies to investigate the nature of dark matter and dark energy across the universe.

name: Psyche
description: Falcon Heavy sent NASA's Psyche spacecraft on a journey to a metal-rich asteroid of the same name, offering scientists a rare look at what may be the exposed core of an early planetary building block.

name: IM-1 (Odysseus Lunar Lander)
description: Falcon 9 launched Intuitive Machines' Odysseus lander toward the Moon, which went on to become the first commercially built spacecraft to achieve a soft lunar landing and the first U.S. lunar touchdown since Apollo.

name: Polaris Dawn
description: A privately funded Crew Dragon mission that flew farther from Earth than any human spaceflight since Apollo and included the first spacewalk performed by a commercial crew.

name: Crew-9 Dragon Mission
description: A NASA Commercial Crew rotation mission that flew astronauts to the International Space Station for a long-duration science expedition aboard Crew Dragon.

name: Starship Integrated Flight Test 5
description: SpaceX achieved the first successful catch of a returning Super Heavy booster using the launch tower's mechanical arms, a major milestone toward rapid vehicle reuse.

name: Starship Integrated Flight Test 6
description: The sixth integrated flight test featured a relit Raptor engine demonstration in space and further refinements to Ship reentry and splashdown, though the booster was diverted to a controlled ocean landing.
